title: Botox Advertising: Examples, Channels and Lead Costs (2026)
summary: Botox advertising for clinics: what live Meta ads show, sample copy, the best channels and how to get Botox leads you can measure. Updated for 2026.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- Good Botox advertising sells the consultation, not the result. It shows the provider, the clinic and the next step, and leaves the outcome implied.
- The ads that keep running on Meta lean on one clear product or treatment, a trust signal such as a review count or a named provider, and a low-pressure call to action.
- Best channels: Google Search for people already looking, Google Business Profile, Instagram and Facebook for reach, and email or text to past patients.
- Measure cost per booked consultation and cost per new patient, not clicks or form fills.


## What live Botox ads show


The[Botox ad wall](https://www.sprites.ai/botox-ads) collects live Meta ads from aesthetic and injectable brands. The page shows 16 advertisers and 425 ads. About 37% of the ads are video. The median ad has run 20 days. The most common call to action is Learn more, on about 34% of ads.


Those numbers say three things. First, most ads are short tests. A 20 day median means advertisers swap creative often, and only a few ads survive. Second, most advertisers still use a soft button. Learn more asks for curiosity, not a commitment. Third, video is a minority format. Static images and short copy carry most of the volume.


The longest-running ads are more useful than the median. The oldest one on the page, at 222 days, opens with a product and a plain benefit: "Complexion Renewal Pads, gentle exfoliation, powerful results." Another that ran 56 days opens with a question the viewer can answer in their head: "Sick of ingrowns and irritation? Ditch the razor for Laser Hair Removal." The rest of the longest runners use a patient story in video, a review count in the first line, a short branded phrase, and a treatment explained in a few words.


What the ads that keep running have in common:


- One product or one treatment per ad, named in the first line.
- A trust signal early, such as a number of 5-star reviews or a named patient or provider.
- A plain benefit stated in everyday words, not a promise about how the viewer will look.
- A single next step, usually to learn more or schedule.


The reason is partly structural. Meta's health and wellness rules mean an ad cannot assert or imply that the viewer has a medical condition, before-and-after images are restricted, and promoting prescription drugs needs Meta's prior approval, so write about the visit and the provider, not the viewer's face.


## The building blocks of a Botox ad


Every Botox ad you write needs the same five parts. Change the wording, keep the order.


Part What to show Example


Hook The treatment and the place Botox consultations in Austin


Provider A named injector with credentials Meet Dana, our nurse injector


Proof Review count, years open, number of patients seen 4.9 stars from 600 reviews


Offer A consultation, a first-visit price or a membership Book a consultation and get a written price


Next step One button Book now or Learn more


Photos matter. Use the treatment room, the front desk, the provider at work, and the product on a tray. Skip stock photos of flawless faces. They look generic, and they run into the same image rules the longest-running ads avoid.


## Sample Botox ads you can adapt


### Facebook and Instagram ad


**Image:** the provider in the treatment room, smiling, no patient face. **Primary text:** "Meet Dana, our nurse injector. Come in for a Botox consultation, ask every question you have, and leave with a written plan and price. No pressure to book a treatment that day." **Headline:** "Botox consultations in Austin." **Button:** Book now.


Swap in your provider, your town and your own consultation terms. Do not copy an offer you do not honor.


### Review-led ad


"Over 600 patients have left us 5 stars. See why neighbors in Round Rock book their Botox with us. Schedule a consultation and meet your injector first." The review count does the persuading, so keep the copy short.


### Google Search ad


Responsive search ads allow up to 15 headlines of 30 characters and 4 descriptions of 90 characters, per Google Ads Help. A starter set:


Element Copy Characters


Headline 1 Botox in Austin 15


Headline 2 Book a Botox Consultation 25


Headline 3 Licensed Nurse Injectors 24


Headline 4 New Patient Pricing 19


Description 1 Meet your injector, ask questions and get a written price. Consultations are free. 82


Each headline should stand alone, because Google mixes them. Match the ad to a landing page that shows the provider, the price range or consultation terms, and a booking form above the fold.


## Which channels work for Botox marketing


1. **Google Search.** The highest-intent channel. People searching "botox near me" or "botox consultation" are close to booking. Bid on your city and nearby towns, and exclude job and training searches.
2. **Google Business Profile.** Photos of the clinic and team, reviews, hours and a booking link. It costs nothing and often decides who gets the call. The[Local Services Ads guide](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/google-local-services-ads) covers Google's pay-per-lead listings, though eligibility depends on service category, so check Google's list.
3. **Instagram and Facebook.** Reach people who are not searching yet. This is where the ads on the wall live. See[Facebook ads for med spas](https://www.sprites.ai/facebook-ads-for-med-spas) for how clinics structure campaigns.
4. **Email and text to past patients.** Botox is a repeat treatment, so your existing list is your cheapest source of bookings. Remind patients when they are due and tell them about new providers or hours.
5. **Referrals and memberships.** A friend-referral card or a membership that includes a discount on repeat visits keeps patients coming back and brings in their friends.


For a wider view, read the[med spa marketing guide](https://www.sprites.ai/med-spa-marketing) , which covers the full set of services a clinic usually sells beside injectables.


## How to get Botox leads you can count


A lead is only useful if someone books. Use a short form: name, phone, the treatment they are asking about, and a preferred day. Do not ask for health details in the ad form. Collect those at intake.


Then answer fast. A lead who submits a form at lunch and hears back that evening has often booked somewhere else. Call or text within minutes during business hours, and set an auto-reply for evenings and weekends that offers a booking link.


## A worked example of Botox lead math


These numbers are an example. Replace them with your own.


Step Number How it is worked out


Monthly ad spend $1,500 Your budget


Cost per lead $30 Spend divided by leads


Leads 50 $1,500 divided by $30


Consultations booked 20 40% of leads


Cost per booked consultation $75 $1,500 divided by 20


New patients treated 12 60% of consultations


Cost per new patient $125 $1,500 divided by 12


First-visit revenue $5,400 12 patients at an average $450


On first-visit revenue alone, $1,500 returns $5,400 in this example. Botox patients usually return, so the lifetime value is higher. Before you scale, check your own booking rate and show rate. If 50 leads produce only 5 consultations, the problem is follow-up, not the ad.


## How to measure a Botox advertising campaign


- Track leads, booked consultations and treated patients by channel.
- Divide spend by booked consultations. That is your cost per consultation.
- Divide spend by new patients. That is your cost to acquire a patient.
- Compare it with average revenue per patient over 12 months.
- Retire an ad when its cost per consultation stays above your target for two weeks, as the 20 day median on the ad wall suggests most advertisers do.


Test one thing at a time: the opening line, the image, or the offer. Keep the winner and write the next test against it.

## FAQ


### What is the best way to advertise Botox?


Use Google Search to reach people already looking, and Instagram and Facebook to reach people who are not. Sell the consultation and the provider, show the clinic, and keep one clear next step. Add email or text to past patients for repeat bookings.


### Can I show before and after photos in Botox ads?


On Meta, before-and-after images are restricted, and the ads should not assert or imply that the viewer has a medical condition. Most clinics show the provider, the treatment room or the product instead, and keep outcome photos for the consultation.


### How much does a Botox lead cost?


It varies by city, offer and ad quality, so use your own numbers. In the worked example above, $30 per lead became $75 per booked consultation and $125 per new patient. Compare cost per new patient with revenue per patient, not the lead cost alone.


### Should Botox ads use video?


Video is useful but not required. On the[Botox ad wall](https://www.sprites.ai/botox-ads) , about 37% of ads are video and the rest are images, and several of the longest-running ads are static. Test a short provider introduction against a simple image.


### What call to action works best for Botox ads?


Learn more is the most common on the ad wall, at about 34% of ads. It is a soft ask. Use Book now when the viewer already knows the clinic, and Learn more when you are introducing a provider or a new treatment.
